angle: the mark or trace the process leaves behind
subject: A sung breath fogged onto a cold window pane, a hatched mass of condensation in the mouth's shape with drops running down from it to the glazing bar.
controls: vowel: shape, the fog's dense core goes from a small round patch (u) to a tall open oval (a) to a wide flat ellipse (i).
breath: scale of the halo only, the sparse outer fog spreads from 1.2× to 2.1× the core while the core stays put.
throat: position, the whole patch sits about 30 px higher on the glass as the throat lengthens (a bigger singer, a mouth higher on the pane).
glide: count, drops gather and run from the bottom of the fog, 2 at 5 ms to 14 at 2 s, each a trail ending in a solid bead.
reference: opxy/craft.md (Semi-opaque areas are hatched, not tinted); opxy/reference/toro-ink-smoke.jpg (steam as a state)
risks: Throat as height on the glass is the weakest mapping of the pass: physical in a story, arbitrary in the sound. A hatched blob needs the window bars to read as fog on glass; without them it's a texture. Many 45° hairlines are costly as nodes and the core's 3 px spacing is at the hatching floor.
